goal: Construir explicación socioecológica multidimensional falsable y simulador como argumento de posibilidad, NO como demostración empírica de comportamiento humano ni originalidad
hypotheses: H0 null: sin preferencias por calidad ni semejanza y oportunidades equilibradas, el sorting no es sistemático
H1 common desirability con thresholds crecientes de calidad puede generar sorting de calidad sin homofilia explícita
H2 exposición segregada genera homogamia de grupo aunque preferencias no contengan semejanza
H3 preferencias explícitas por semejanza pueden explicar el mismo patrón con mecanismo distinto
H4 ranking platform centrado en popularidad redistribuye exposición y concentración aun con igual presupuesto de visualizaciones por emisor
H5 filtros de reciprocidad y matching alteran selección/coverage de forma no intercambiable
H6 efectos de feedback privado de rechazo frente a reputación pública son intervenciones distintas y no observadas en humanos

H7 dimension cultural, normativa, institucional, edad, generacional, orientación, terceros, valores ideales y continuidad de relación requieren instrumentos adicionales; no generalizar el simulador heterosexual

fixed_params.sex_groups: M/F abstract binary only, deliberately not a universal representation of relationships
fixed_params.k_per_right: 12 in regular modes, NOT equal in popularity skew
fixed_params.quality_distribution: Uniform(0,1) independent of field and age
fixed_params.mutual_choice_noise: pre-generated pair-specific uniforms to share random potential outcomes across scenarios
fixed_params.decision_utility: logit intercept -0.35 + 2*quality_weight*(q_target-.5) + homophily_weight*field_same -0.7*reservation_gradient*(q_actor-.5), when both see each other; negative control constant
fixed_params.durability: optional stage with probability depending on age gap and field; NOT trained on human data
fixed_params.matching: Maximum cardinality bipartite matching on reciprocal candidates using scipy.sparse.csgraph.maximum_bipartite_matching; no unique stable matching claim
fixed_params.exposure_regular: 12 independent perfect-matchings with groupwise randomized switches avoiding duplicate edges
fixed_params.exposure_group: degree-preserving 2x2 switches favor same field; diagnostic edge changes and bipartite degrees
fixed_params.popularity_exposure: each LEFT chooser gets 12 candidate impressions weighted by target q, RIGHT receives unequal number; asymmetry explicitly audited

adversarial: same-group exposure with zero same-group preference
common quality with and without quality-correlated acceptance threshold
vary k with same agents and compare opportunity budget explicitly
report negatives and Monte Carlo uncertainty n=6 not population inference
methodology.pass_condition: all 7 named conditions run 6 seeds, invariants verified: max degree/per side, dyads no duplicates, match subset mutual, match monogamous, coverage consistent
methodology.no_auto_upgrade: zero human validation, level 0/3 or at most local 1/3 methodological if genuinely nontrivial and unreported, never 2/3
methodology.R5: If toy model reproduces known prior art only, stop after enough diagnostic contrasts instead of spending remaining slots on more synthetic tuning.

cycle_contract.goal: Theoretical and bibliographic atlas across preferences, third parties, opportunity, technology, sex/sexual orientation, cultural values, temporal search, socioeconomic strata; source registry updates mandatory.
Structural causal DAG/SCM, mathematical stage selection decomposition, identifiable vs unidentifiable causal claims, fidelity audit and model capability matrix.
Implement and run frozen null control, check zero artificial sorting under balanced random opportunity.
Show assortativity through same-group opportunities without explicit homophily, fixed degrees, two-sided opportunity graph.
Compare common quality, status-dependent reservations, explicit same-group preference and mixed version, pair seeds.
Popularity-weighted candidate display, unequal right visibility despite constant left budget; inequality and coverage.
Distinguish exposure, reciprocal yes, match and optional durability with denominators; joint outcome selection and no causal claims.
Vary opportunity budget (k=6 or24), subgroup composition, asymmetric sex ratio and model scope; only count cases actually executed.
Competent alternative mechanisms, compare data source constraints, revise priors, model limitations, final R5 and CT2.

prior_grades.prior_novelty: Strong prior art for generic assortativity without homophily, especially Topinkova-Diviak 2025, Kalmijn 1998, Chen 2023

external_data: No new human sample at this prereg stage
privacy: No patient/real person rows, only synthetic outputs
